summary: Describes the LDAP / X.500 entryDN operational attribute, which gives a copy of an entry's distinguished name for use in attribute value assertions. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: A directory entry that carries a copy of its own full address so you can search by it.

questions: what is the ldap entrydn attribute
what is an ldap distinguished name
how to search ldap by dn
subtitle: An LDAP attribute that holds a copy of an entry's distinguished name so searches can test it.

tldr.problem: An entry's distinguished name (DN) is not one of its attributes, so it is not possible to run attribute value assertions against it.
tldr.mechanism: The 'entryDN' operational attribute is a single-valued, read-only copy of the entry's current DN, which can be used in search filters.
tldr.outcome: Searches can restrict results by DN, for example to return entries from two chosen subtrees only. The attribute has the OID 1.3.6.1.1.20.

today: RFC 5020 is a Proposed Standard. It has not been obsoleted or updated according to the metadata for this RFC.

sections.title: Background and Intended Use
sections.content:
In X.500 directory services, including those reached with LDAP, an entry is identified by its distinguished name (DN). The DN is not an attribute of the entry, so you cannot run attribute value assertions against it.

This RFC defines the entryDN operational attribute, which holds a copy of the entry's DN. It may be used in search filters. The RFC's example searches the subtree dc=example,dc=com with a component match on entryDN and returns entries under ou=A,dc=example,dc=com and ou=B,dc=example,dc=com, but no other entries in that subtree.
sections.eli5: Searching is easier when the full address is written on the card itself. This note puts it there.

sections.title: The entryDN Attribute
sections.content:
The attribute provides a copy of the entry's current DN. Its schema definition gives it the OID 1.3.6.1.1.20, the matching rule distinguishedNameMatch, the syntax 1.3.6.1.4.1.1466.115.121.1.12, and marks it SINGLE-VALUE, NO-USER-MODIFICATION and USAGE directoryOperation.

Because of NO-USER-MODIFICATION, the DN of the entry cannot be changed through this attribute.
sections.eli5: The copy is read only. You can look at it, but writing on it does not rename anyone.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The attribute only provides an additional way to access an entry's DN. The RFC therefore does not believe that it introduces new security considerations.
sections.eli5: The address was already there to find. A copy of it does not let anyone see anything new.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA has registered an LDAP object identifier for the attribute type and the LDAP descriptor entryDN. The descriptor maps to the object identifier 1.3.6.1.1.20, with usage "Attribute Type", specification RFC 5020 and the IESG as change controller.
sections.eli5: The name and number of the new attribute were written in an official list so nobody else uses them.
